text.title: Python FastAPI — Failure Modes
text.summary: Nine antipatterns observed when python-fastapi is mis-applied, each with symptom, root cause, and concrete fix.

antipattern.description: One AsyncSession passed to multiple coroutines in asyncio.gather.
antipattern.reason: Root cause: Concurrent use corrupts session state; rare race conditions in prod. Fix: One session per coroutine — get a new one inside each task via Depends.

antipattern.description: ORM queries + business logic + serialisation all inside the route function.
antipattern.reason: Root cause: Untestable without HTTP; logic duplicated across endpoints. Fix: Move to service function; route stays thin.
Root cause: Worker process exhausts under load; response latency spikes. Fix: Move to Celery/Arq/Taskiq; return 202 Accepted.
Root cause: Field renames ship to production without anyone noticing. Fix: Snapshot the schema; fail CI on diff without bump.

Root cause: Copied from a pre-0.93 tutorial and never migrated; FastAPI emits a DeprecationWarning at boot and the hooks will be removed. Fix: One `@asynccontextmanager async def lifespan(app)` doing setup, `yield`, teardown, passed as `FastAPI(lifespan=lifespan)`. Rule r7-lifespan-not-on-event.

antipattern.description: One Pydantic model reused for create, update and response.
antipattern.reason: Root cause: Writing four classes felt like boilerplate. Symptom: clients can set `id` and `created_at` on create, the response schema advertises `password`, and PATCH requires fields the caller did not want to change. Fix: Base / Create / Update / Response, with `ConfigDict(from_attributes=True)` on Response. Rule r8-schema-quartet.

antipattern.description: Synchronous I/O inside an async route — `requests.get(...)`, a sync `Session.query(...)`, a blocking file read.
antipattern.reason: Root cause: A sync client was in scope and the call looked harmless. Symptom: throughput is fine in a single-user test and collapses under concurrency, because the blocking call holds the event loop and every other request queues behind it. Fix: `httpx.AsyncClient` and `AsyncSession` + `await db.execute(select(...))`; wrap genuinely blocking libraries in `run_in_threadpool`. Rule r12-no-sync-io-in-async-route.

antipattern.description: `/docs`, `/redoc` and `/openapi.json` served in production with no environment guard.
antipattern.reason: Root cause: The defaults were never overridden. Symptom: the full API surface — every route, parameter and schema — is readable by anyone who finds the host. Fix: `docs_url="/docs" if settings.debug else None` (and the same for redoc/openapi), with settings loaded from cached `BaseSettings`. Rule r13-guard-docs-in-prod.
